newsitem.title: INDIA: Office tower in India's Bombay hit by fire.
newsitem.headline: Office tower in India's Bombay hit by fire.

text.p: Twenty-one people were rescued from a fire in a 25-storey building in India's financial capital Bombay on Wednesday and the blaze was under control, officials said. There were no reported casualties.
Shridhar Joshi, additional municipal commissioner told Reuters the fire was under control and that 21 people had been rescued.
He said authorities would have to wait for smoke to clear to confirm no one was injured.
"We can't rule out the possibility of more people being there (in the building)," he said.
Officials at the 25-storey Express Towers said the fire apparently broke out on the 21st floor. Sixteen fire engines battled to control the fire, they said.

"It appears the fire started on the 21st floor," a member of the Goenka family, which owns the building, told Reuters from the nearby Oberoi Hotel. Officials said earlier that the fire was on the 13th floor.
"Firemen are all over the place and most of it is put out already," she said but did not want to be identified.
She said Vivek Goenka, who controls the Indian Express newspaper group, was at the building overseeing operations.

"I was working in my office at 8.20 (a.m.) (0250 GMT) on the 22nd floor," said Roshan Sabhu, who works for pharmaceutical firm Pfizer Ltd. "It was 8.22 when I heard the fire alarm bells and I came down by lift with a colleague and six canteen boys."
He said he saw the Goenka family, who stay on the top floor penthouse, alight from another elevator.
The building, in the prestigious Nariman Point business district, houses offices of the Express newspaper group and those of local and foreign firms and banks.
